segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What is to speak?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablar, -ar verb. And to eat?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Comer.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comer, -er verb. And to live?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vivir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vivir, -ir verb. Good. So there we have an -ar, -er, and -ir verb. And we saw -ar verbs form one group and -er, -ir verbs form another group. But we have one time in the entire Spanish language where there is a difference between -er and -ir verbs. Otherwise they're always forming one group. But just one occasion in the whole Spanish language where there is a difference between them.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How do you say we speak, or we are speaking?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablamos. How would you say we eat, or we are eating?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Comemos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comemos. Good. And how is we live?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vivimos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vivimos. Good. So for -er verbs we use -emos for "we" in the present, and for -ir verbs we use -imos for "we" in the present. But of course for the other versions they are using the same endings. For example, he eats is

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Come.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Come. We use -e. He lives

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vive.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vive. Again, we're using an -e. They eat or you guys eat?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Comen.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. They live or you guys live?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Viven.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Viven. Where do you guys live?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Dónde viven?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Dónde viven? Very good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What was the word for "it"? Not "eat", but "it", i-t.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo. Good. There's a couple of interesting and useful things we can do with "lo" - "it" in Spanish which we can't do in English. For example, when you want to say the interesting thing, the complicated thing is, the interesting thing is, the difficult thing about that is, instead of saying the word for "thing" in Spanish, you can just say, for example, "lo interesante". "Lo interesante" means the interesting thing. Huh? So you get the structure "the interesting thing" with "lo interesante". So,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: how would you say, for example, the interesting thing is that they live here? The interesting thing is that they live here.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo interesante es que viven aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Lo interesante es que viven aquí. Very good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say the interesting thing is that they live together? Now, the word for "together" in Spanish is junto. Junto.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Junto.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: This is the singular masculine version. J-u-n-t-o. Now, it's related to "junction". It doesn't sound like it, but when you realize that junto is with "j", then you can see how it's related to junction in English and "join".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The interesting thing is that they live together.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo interesante es que viven junto...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, but it's them, no? They viven

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: juntos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Lo interesante es que viven juntos. Or if they were two females, you would say

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Juntas.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Lo interesante es que viven juntas. The interesting thing is that they live together.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What do you think fácil means? Fácil.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Easy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Easy. Why?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Facilitate?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Facilitate. Good. To facilitate is to make easy. So we have fácil, easy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if you wanted to say the easy thing, how would you say that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo fácil.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo fácil, and then you will carry on. So we can say, the easy thing is that they come together. The easy thing is that they come together.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo fácil es que... Venir is irregular, right?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Try and build it. See what happens. Go there first, and then see.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: It's not vieno. No, it's vengo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But you're going for the "they" version, so don't go from venir to "I" version to "they" version.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: But I might as well remember it.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Why?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: That's how you'll get lost. Ah, right? What you want to do is focus your thoughts on just what you have in front of you, which is going from venir to the "they" form, and try to build it as it should be, and then when you get that result, then have a look at, oh, maybe if it's irregular, if it doesn't feel right.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So is it vienen?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Of course. You see?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: The "I" one though, my mind is trying to remember.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vengo.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vengo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But it's not important. If you don't need it now, it shouldn't be important for you. Because with everything you will remember, you will remember something similar that you don't remember. If you let that occupy your thoughts, then you are going to block. You need to be comfortable with a level of uncertainty to learn a language. If you want to have the whole panorama of the whole language before you start speaking, you will never start speaking. And sooner or later we're going to come across again that thought that distracted us because we're going to want to say it, and in that moment we will sort it out. So the more we do that, the more you're going to control this panorama of Spanish that makes you a little bit insecure right now because you know so much and you feel like it's all floating around.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The easy thing is that they come together.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo fácil es que vienen juntos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Lo fácil es que vienen juntos. Very good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say the complicated thing is that they come together?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Complicación, complicar, complicado?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So... Lo complicado es que vienen juntos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo complicado es que vienen juntos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So we can say lo bueno, the good thing, lo malo, the bad thing - malo is bad like in malnourished, that means badly nourished. So that's a useful structure.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Before we said de esta forma, in this way, de esta forma. We can also say de esta manera, in this manner.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But very, very common in Spanish when we want to say like this, like that, is the word así. A-s-i. Así.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Así means like this or like that. So if you want to say something like we don't speak like this, we don't speak in that way, you don't really need to say de esa manera or de esa forma. You can just take this wonderful shortcut for like this or like that, which is así. So like this, like that, así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, we don't speak like that. We don't speak in that way.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No hablamos así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No hablamos así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We don't eat like that.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No comemos así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No comemos así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We don't live like that.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No vivimos así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No vivimos así. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Another interesting thing that we can do with lo, a useful structure we can make with lo, is lo de. The combination of lo and de means like "the thing about". So we're seeing how lo can sometimes replace "thing", lo interesante, the interesting thing, and lo de is like "the thing about". So, for example, if you wanted to say the thing about the party, you'd just say lo de la fiesta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if you want to say we are speaking about the thing about the party, not we are speaking about the party, but we're speaking about that issue of the party, that thing we know what we are referring to, we are speaking about that business about the party. Hablamos lo de la fiesta, or hablamos sobre, about, you could say that as well, hablamos sobre lo de la fiesta, you could even say de, we speak of, hablamos de lo de la fiesta.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: You can say that business about Juan, that thing about Juan. How would you say that?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo de Juan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Ah, lo de Juan. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So you could say, I don't want to speak about Juan's business like this. I don't want to speak about Juan's business like this. And for Juan's business you will just say

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo de Juan.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, I don't want to speak about Juan's business like this?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No quiero hablar de lo de Juan así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. No quiero hablar de lo de Juan así. Or we could say no quiero hablar sobre lo de Juan así, or just no quiero hablar lo de Juan así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So lo de we kind of want to see as a unit meaning that thing about, and we've seen already that de can mean about, so it's just it about, that thing about. It's used very often in Spanish and you will find it very useful.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So you could say, for example, I want to organize that thing tomorrow. That thing tomorrow, the thing about tomorrow, ah? I want to organize - what's to organize?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Organizar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, I want to organize that thing about tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero organizar lo de la mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: La mañana is the morning.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Oh, sorry. Tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yeah, so morning and tomorrow are the same word in Spanish, mañana. If you say la mañana, we're going to understand the morning.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So it's just mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So all together?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Quiero organizar lo de mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Quiero organizar lo de mañana. It about tomorrow, the thing about tomorrow. Quiero organizar lo de mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But I don't want to organize it like this. But I don't want to organize it like this.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Pero no quiero organizarlo así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Pero no quiero organizarlo así. Good. But I don't want to organize it like this. Or if you wanted to be more emphatic, you could replace así with de esta manera, de esta forma, of this way, of this form. But así is the most common. You will be hearing it all the time.
